services/control-plane/bff/downstream_he: Delivery age bound (PANTHEON_BFF_HEALTH_DELIVERY_MAX_AGE_SECONDS, default 21600): each drain first moves pending, retry and expired-claim rows whose updated_at is older than the bound to status quarantined and releases opening/resolving incident mappings they held; quarantined is counted in delivery counts and excluded from backlog.

claim_due excludes rows with undelivered dependencies inside the SQL query (json_each), so a blocked oldest window no longer starves newer rows; the Python-side _dependencies_delivered filter is removed.
incident_resolve is queued only on the opening/open -> resolving transition.

publish_loop_12_controller_truth imports services.loop-control explicitly, keeps the heartbeat task reference, and records published/failed/unconfigured with a DSN-redacted error in get_state()['loop_12_controller_truth'].
replay_dead_letters without an explicit event_id redrives only dead letters created inside the age bound; an explicit event_id can still redrive an older row.
changes.services/control-plane/bff/core/lifespan: create_lifespan starts the downstream health monitor (explicit argument, otherwise the instance its constructor registered) after startup wiring and stops it on shutdown; app.state.downstream_health_monitor exposes it.
changes.services/control-plane/bff/control_loops: The dead-letter replay route runs the monitor's synchronous drain in a worker thread instead of on the event loop.
changes.main.py: Not edited; the composition root already constructs and registers exactly one monitor.

hosted_backlog_handling: This task performs no hosted action: no hosted queue was replayed, purged or quarantined. When an exact-pair release containing this change starts the BFF, the first drain quarantines pending/retry rows with no delivery activity inside the age bound (the 2026-10-06 hosted ledger held about 170k such rows) and keeps them in the ledger for audit; dead_letter rows stay dead_letter; replay without event_id only redrives recent dead letters.
